newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed as yield curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed as yield curve steepens.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed in light trade on Thursday, with the yield curve steepening amid a weaker-than-expected retail sales report, analysts said.

"The action in the short end I think is a reaction to recent numbers," said Barry Allan, vice-president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Services. "The retail sales numbers were quite weak. That certainly implies there is the potential for further easing by the Bank of Canada."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.12 to C$115.30 to yield 6.752 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 5/32 to yield 6.42 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds narrowed to 33 basis points from 34 basis points at Wednesday's close.

Short-term Canadian bonds were firmer after Statistics Canada reported that retail sales rose 0.2 percent in September to a seasonally adjusted C$17.93 billion from an upwardly revised C$17.89 billion in August, Statistics Canada said. Economists had forecast sales would rise by 0.4 percent in September.
The report, which also prompted strength in T-bills, increased optimism among traders that the Bank of Canada's November 8 rate cut will not be the last of this year.

Canada's better performance relative to U.S. bonds at the long end may be the result of Canada-U.S. spread narrowing trades, said Allan. Such trades sent the 30-year spread to an 11 year low of 20 basis points earlier this month before stalling.
"The cheapest part of the Canadian curve is the long end relative to the U.S.," said Allan

In new issue news, the Government of Canada said it plans to auction on November 27 C$400 million of 4.25 percent real return bonds maturing on December 1, 2026. The bonds are in addition to C$1.45 billion of real return bonds due Dec 2026 already outstanding.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.18 to C$106.35 to yield 6.141 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 2/32 to yield 6.14 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was close to zero, almost unchanged from Wednesday's close.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.84 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.16 percent.
